>>259014402
The more I read the excerpts from what Ted has written the more I find myself to be like-minded to what he has written. I would feel as if I could eventually even come up with those claims myself if they hadn't been already written. That being said I look forward to reading some if not all of it.

>They are not the results of chance but are IMPOSED on him by other persons whose decisions he, as an individual, is unable to influence.
>But threats to the modern individual tend to be MAN-MADE.

>You will live to see man-made horrors beyond your comprehension.

I tend to make comparisons to the issue with trans people a lot because of how the man-made horror they themselves have casted upon themselves affects other people.
A bakery has been sued for rejecting to bake a cake for both a gay and trans people; for their wedding or whatnot.
The bakery was attacked by "other persons whose decisions it was unable to influence" and given the all destructive labels of a homophobic / transphobic bakery.
The result was practically nuking down the salary of it to the point where the owner has practically went bankrupt.
Although not the best example it may be, it's just one of the many on how the modern world - and the progress of technology that has also allowed for the horrors to be created in the first place - is not going in a right direction.
In fact, it never was. Only a small part of the current technology could be in fact kept; given it's used for the right purposes. However, the purpose of the rest had a destructive effect on civilization as a whole - and the only progress noticed is by those that were never free thinkers in the first place.
